Argentine Firm Unveils Smart Metering Technology for Gas and Water Utilities

BUENOS AIRES, June 13 — A leading Argentine technology supplier launched a new line of smart metering solutions for the country’s gas and water utilities on Thursday, aiming to modernize infrastructure and improve efficiency across the sector.

The company, InfraSoluciones SA, presented its “AquaGas Smart” platform at a press event in Buenos Aires attended by utility representatives, government officials, and industry analysts. The new devices, designed to be installed by local utility providers, use advanced sensors and wireless communication to monitor consumption in real-time and detect leaks or irregularities.

“This is a significant step forward for Argentina’s utilities,” said InfraSoluciones CEO Mariana Cárdenas. “With AquaGas Smart, providers and customers alike will benefit from more accurate billing, early detection of issues, and greater transparency in resource management.”

Argentina’s gas and water networks, much of which date back to the mid-20th century, have long faced challenges with aging infrastructure and non-technical losses. Industry observers say the adoption of smart metering systems has been slower than in some neighboring countries. According to the Argentine Association of Public Services (AAPS), less than 10% of residential connections are currently equipped with advanced metering infrastructure.

“With this launch, we hope to accelerate the digital transformation in the sector,” Cárdenas added. She noted the company had already signed pilot agreements with water utility Aguas Pampeanas and gas distributor MetroGas Sur, covering approximately 30,000 households in Buenos Aires and La Pampa provinces.

Government officials welcomed the development, seeing it as a boost for efficiency and environmental stewardship. “Smart meters can help reduce water losses and gas leaks, which is critical as we face increasing demands on our resources,” said Undersecretary for Energy Transition Juan Pablo Rossi at the event. “We are committed to supporting the modernization of utility infrastructure through regulatory and financial incentives.”

Analysts say the rollout of smart technologies could also open new opportunities for local manufacturing and software development. “There’s potential for job creation and technology exports if Argentine firms can establish themselves in this niche,” said Gabriela Torres, an industry consultant.

InfraSoluciones said commercial deployments would begin in the third quarter, with plans to expand availability nationwide by 2025.
